newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Congress to mull 600,000-job plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Congress to mull 600,000-job plan - paper.

text.p: Argentina's lower house of Congress will debate Wednesday a $1.2 billion plan proposed by members of the ruling Peronist Party to create 600,000 jobs, the Clarin newspaper reported Monday.
The plan is being backed by Peronist Chamber of Deputies chief Jorge Matzkin, Clarin said, quoting Congressional sources.
It was not immediately possible to contact any Peronist congressional spokesman.
Under the plan, the government would stimulate the creation of 600,000 jobs by granting companies taking on workers a $200 monthly subsidy, the state-controlled Telam news agency reported.

The money for the subsidy would come from a fund financed by a bond issue, which would be guaranteed by money owed to the government by companies who have deferred tax payments under industrial promotion schemes.
"It is vital to create this trust fund to stimulate the creation of 600,000 jobs for heads of family who are jobless today," Peronist Congressman Oscar Lamberto told Telam.
Argentina's economy has returned to strong growth after a deep recession in 1994, but the latest figures showed unemployment still at 17.3 percent last October.
With mid-term congressional elections looming in October, sometimes violent protests have broken out in many parts of Argentina over the last few months by demonstrators calling for work.

But the government of President Carlos Menem -- which has agreed strict deficit targets with the International Monetary Fund -- has so far shied away from spending public money to create jobs. Instead it has pinned its hopes for lower unemployment on economic growth and passing new laws to make labor contracts more flexible.
